title: Cross-region failover handoff and KV-cache checklist (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft for handing off cross-region failover during a region-level outage. Focus areas: DNS routing changes, weighted traffic shifts, warm-standby capacity verification, KV-cache/redis priming and consistency, database read-replica checks, and short-term rollback criteria.

Context / when to use this doc:
- Primary region degraded or isolated (network partition, AZ-correlated outage) and an SRE lead decides to shift production traffic to the warm standby region.
- Not intended for total global control-plane outage — follow emergency exec playbook in that case.

Assumptions about our infra (current as of Feb 2026):
- Traffic is routed with CloudDNS (high-level weighted records) and global load balancers in front of regional clusters.
- Each region runs a set of GPU-backed inference pods behind regional ingress and an edge CDN for static content.
- Warm standby region has scaled base capacity (~30–40% of peak) and accepts traffic after a controlled ramp.
- Redis-based KV cache per region with prefix/KV caching and cross-region fallback to cold cache if keys missing.
- Database: primary writes in primary region; asynchronous replicas in warm-standby region (replication lag target < 5s under normal ops).
- Conventions: TTLs for DNS records set to 60s for critical endpoints, 300s for non-critical.

Checklist: Immediate triage (first 10 minutes)
- Confirm symptoms and scope: which endpoints, latency/error patterns, and regions reporting failures. (oncall -> slack #sre-oncall incident thread)
- Attach incident ticket: JIRA ID (create if missing).
- Verify that control plane is reachable from a different region (run quick curl from ci-runner in secondary region).
- Check Cloud provider status page for known outages (link in incident thread).

Capacity & warm-standby validation (10–25 minutes)
- Run these commands (or Dashboard shortcuts) to validate warm-standby health:
  - kubectl --context=warm-standby get pods -n inference | grep CrashLoopBackOff
  - kubectl --context=warm-standby top nodes (verify CPU/GPU pressure)
  - Check autoscaler status and pending scale-up events in cloud console
- Verify model files and weights availability in warm-standby registry/storage: ls /mnt/models/<model-version> or S3 ls s3://models/production/<model-version>
- Confirm inference runtime version matches production (runtime vX.Y.Z). If mismatched, note risk and consider using compatible model variant.

KV-cache & prefix caching (critical)
- Goal: prevent mass cold cache storms that 10x request latency and crash GPUs on initial swell.
- Steps:
  1) Check regional redis metrics: hit-rate, memory, evictions (Grafana: redis-kv-standby:hit_rate)
  2) If hit-rate < 70%, do NOT flip 100% traffic. Instead, perform staged canary (see Traffic ramping).
  3) If we have recent cache dump snapshots (kv-snapshots/<region>/latest), trigger restore to warm-standby redis. Command: redis-cli --rdb /tmp/restore.rdb then restart redis with restored rdb (ops-only).
  4) If restores are not available, prepare to prime cache with top-N prefixes: use backfill script s3://runbooks/priming/top-prefixes-7d.json and run in low concurrency mode (concurrency=4).
  5) Note: while priming, set a short-lived rate limit on user-facing endpoints to prevent cascade.

Database / replication sanity (15–35 minutes)
- Check replica lag (DB monitoring dashboard). If replica lag > 30s, warm-standby region is not safe for writes-dependent flows.
- For read-heavy endpoints, it's acceptable to shift reads if lag under 60s, but validate data consistency via sample queries (select last 10 user events for 5 sample accounts).
- If writes must be allowed in standby, coordinate promotion procedure with DB lead (manual promotion required; follow DB promotion runbook).

DNS and traffic shifting (25–60 minutes)
- Preferred path: weighted DNS + load balancer config change + canary traffic. Do not immediately swap authoritative records.
- Steps:
  1) Reduce TTLs (if currently >60s) — do this preemptively in maintenance windows. If already >60s during incident, be aware of propagation delay.
  2) Using CloudDNS console, change weight: primary_region 80 -> 50, warm-standby 20 -> 50 (example). Make small incremental moves: 10%, 30%, 60%, 100%.
  3) After each step wait 60–120 seconds and monitor: 5xx rate, P50/P95 latency, GPU queue length, redis hit-rate in both regions.
  4) If errors spike in standby when increasing weight, immediately roll back to previous stable weight.
  5) If provider supports geo-routing fallback, enable region-based routing (route by source IP) as a last resort for latency-sensitive customers.

Traffic ramping / canary plan
- Canary group size and selection:
  - Canary 1: internal traffic from CI and non-customer test tokens — 1–5%
  - Canary 2: low-SLA customers / small API keys — 5–20%
  - Canary 3: public traffic gradually to 100% if metrics acceptable
- Metrics to watch during canary (define acceptable thresholds in incident):
  - 5xx rate increase <= 1% absolute
  - P95 latency increase <= 200ms
  - Redis miss-rate change <= 10% relative
  - GPU queue length < 300 (or region-specific SLO)
- If any threshold breaches, pause and run rollback checklist.

Rollback checklist (immediate revert)
- Revert DNS weights to last known-good distribution.
- Drain warm-standby ingress and redirect health-checks back to primary.
- If KV priming scripts are running, stop and purge any partially applied primed keys (note the side-effects) and notify data team.
- Post an update on incident thread with exact rollback time and reason.

Operational communication
- Incident commander updates every 15 minutes to #sre-oncall and #eng-incident-briefing.
- Status page: operations -> set status: degraded / region outage / partial outage. Use standard templated message (see linked_artifacts).
- Customer-facing timeline: first update within 30 minutes, then every 60 minutes. Prep an internal FAQ for CS and AE teams with likely questions.

Handoff to next shift / post-handoff notes (before handing off)
- Ensure ticket contains: actions taken, current DNS weights, cache priming status, replica lag, and model-serving health snapshots.
- Produce a short checklist for oncoming shift: next weight step, expected metric targets, who to page (oncall escalation list).
- Save ephemeral URLs and command history in the ticket (we use runkit snippet or incident-runbook log).

Post-incident follow-up items (postmortem candidates)
- If any manual priming was necessary, investigate automation for periodic cross-region snapshotting of top prefixes.
- Evaluate whether warm-standby should be kept at higher baseline capacity for specific high-risk models.
- Improve telemetry: add live KV priming progress dashboard and a single view of cross-region redis hit rates.
- Add automated canary rollback triggers when P95 latency crosses a threshold for >2 consecutive minutes.

Troubles, WIP items, and open questions
- WIP: cross-region redis snapshot restore currently requires manual ops steps and causes a brief restart window. Need runbook for zero-downtime restore (Priya Nair).
- Open question: should we support transparent read-after-write consistency for small bounded windows when failing over? (DB team input required).
- Known gap: session stickiness implementation varies across clouds; we need a single abstraction layer.

Quick reference commands (ops shortcuts)
- Check replica lag: curl -s https://db-metrics.internal/replica-lag | jq .lag_seconds
- Redis hit-rate: kubectl --context=warm-standby exec -n monitoring prometheus-query -- "avg(rate(redis_key_hits[5m])) / avg(rate(redis_commands_total[5m]))"
- Set CloudDNS weight (example CLI): gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=prod && gcloud dns record-sets transaction remove --name api.example.com. --type A --ttl=60 --zone=prod --addresses <old-ip> && gcloud dns record-sets transaction add --name api.example.com. --type A --ttl=60 --zone=prod --addresses <new-ip> && gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=prod

Notes to self (informal)
- Don't forget to check CDN edge error rates — sometimes the problem is cache invalidation, not origin.
- We should keep a small pool of pre-warmed model containers in warm-standby for the top-10 customer models.
- Document exact model-weights compatibility table in Confluence (link in linked_artifacts).

Immediate next steps (for today)
- Triage ticket JIRA-SRE-1127 -> categorize as regional-outage if not already.
- Run basic warm-standby health checks and post results to incident thread.
- If priming needed, schedule priming job with "low-concurrency" flag and monitor.

End of draft. Please comment inline, add playbook tweaks, and flag any missed edge-cases.

References and useful links:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-REGION-FAILOVER-PLAYBOOK
- Incident runbook template: runbooks/reroute-template.md
- Cache priming script: s3://runbooks/priming/
summary: Working draft runbook for controlled cross-region failover focusing on DNS weight shifts, warm-standby capacity checks, KV-cache priming, read-replica validation, canary ramps, rollback criteria, and post-incident follow-up.
